references.text: Isaiah urges us to share bread with the hungry and bring homeless wanderers into our homes — acts of charity and mercy that cleanse and honor God ([ref:Jes 58:7|Isaiah 58:7]).
Whoever shows kindness to the poor lends to the Lord — giving alms is an act that God values ([ref:Ordsp 19:17|Proverbs 19:17]).
Daniel advises King Nebuchadnezzar to redeem his sins with righteousness and his wrongdoings with mercy toward the poor — almsgiving as a means of cleansing ([ref:Dan 4:27|Daniel 4:27]).
Jesus encourages his disciples to sell what they own and give alms — giving to the poor as an expression of genuine reverence for God ([ref:Luk 12:33|Luke 12:33]).

The immediate context: Jesus rebukes the Pharisees for cleaning the outside of cups and dishes while inside they are full of greed and wickedness — outward purity without inner purity is hypocrisy ([ref:Luk 11:39-40|Luke 11:39-40]).

Matthew's parallel account where Jesus accuses the scribes and Pharisees of cleaning the outside of cups and dishes, but inside they are full of greed and excess ([ref:Matt 23:25-26|Matthew 23:25-26]).
"All things are clean to those who are clean" — Paul's principle reflecting Jesus' words that when the inner person is pure, everything is pure ([ref:Tit 1:15|Titus 1:15]).
Whoever has a generous eye (a giving attitude) will be blessed, for he gives of his bread to the poor — generosity as an expression of a pure heart ([ref:Ordsp 22:9|Proverbs 22:9]).

Cornelius gave generously in alms to the people and prayed continually to God, and his gifts rose up as a memorial offering before God — almsgiving as a sign of a pure heart ([ref:Apg 10:2-4|Acts 10:2-4]).
The Lord calls us to wash ourselves, cleanse ourselves, learn to do good, seek justice, and help the oppressed — inner cleansing through righteous actions ([ref:Jes 1:16-17|Isaiah 1:16-17]).
Micah summarizes what the Lord requires: to act justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with God — the inner and moral over the outer and ritual ([ref:Mi 6:8|Micah 6:8]).
